description: Baseline: relancers RLNC encode/decode/recode

asi.bottleneck: Per-byte field element conversions in encode_symbol and symbol scale/add operations

description: Loop interchange in encode_symbol: iterate symbols outer, bytes inner

asi.hypothesis: Reorganizing encode_symbol to process each symbol sequentially (scaled + XOR) instead of strided byte-by-byte accumulation improves cache locality
asi.next_action_hint: Try removing zero-byte/branch guards in scale_byte; explore packed field operations for bulk processing
asi.bottleneck: Per-byte field conversions remain dominant despite better memory access pattern

description: Remove zero-byte early-exit guard in Symbol::scale

asi.hypothesis: On random data, the branch misprediction cost of `if byte == 0` exceeds the savings from skipping multiplication
asi.next_action_hint: Explore packed field bulk operations (PackedAESBinaryField16x8b) for 16x throughput

description: Add precomputed AES GF(2^8) multiplication table + fast path in Symbol::scale

asi.hypothesis: Precomputed 256x256 multiplication table turns field multiply into a single cache lookup, bypassing binius scalar packed-field overhead
asi.bottleneck: encode_symbol still clones each symbol before scaling; need in-place scale_add_assign
asi.next_action_hint: Add in-place scale_add_assign to avoid per-symbol clone; apply table to decoder/recode paths

description: Loop unroll scale_add_assign_aes by 8x; remove redundant init_matrix in decode; lazy partial symbols
SSSE3 split-table SIMD for AES GF(2^8) mul using _mm_shuffle_epi8
AVX2 split-table SIMD (256-bit _mm256_shuffle_epi8) for AES GF(2^8)
AVX-512VBMI split-table SIMD (512-bit _mm512_shuffle_epi8) for AES GF(2^8)
Fast-path coefficient generation for AES (fill_bytes instead of F::random); raw-byte matrix ops in decoder (neutral)

asi.hypothesis: Speed up coefficient generation for AESTowerField8b by using fill_bytes instead of per-element F::random. Also try raw-byte coefficient matrix in decoder to avoid transmute_copy overhead.
asi.decoder_raw_byte_result: Neutral to slightly worse (0.234ms -> 0.236ms), likely because transmute_copy on u8 is already free and the raw pointer cast adds aliasing concerns
asi.rng_fast_path_result: Encode improved from 0.0188ms to 0.0169ms (~10% win) by using ChaCha8Rng::fill_bytes for AES coefficients

description: #[inline(always)] on SIMD wrappers + scale_add_assign_aes (no improvement)

asi.hypothesis: Force inlining of SIMD wrappers and scale_add_assign_aes to eliminate function call overhead in decode hot loop
asi.result: No improvement - compiler was already inlining the hot paths; function symbols in nm are dead code kept for COMDAT
asi.next_action_hint: Decode overhead is not in function call overhead but in L1 cache capacity (64KB working set > 48KB L1d) and lack of GFNI. Focus on algorithmic changes or in-place symbol processing

description: Avoid push+clone in gaussian_elimination symbol selection; use ptr::write into pre-allocated Vec
Avoid 512KB copy in decode() by transmuting Vec<Symbol<M>> into Vec<u8> via from_raw_parts; also fix generic path to use separate Vec<F> matrix

asi.hypothesis: The final copy from Vec<Symbol<M>> to Vec<u8> in decode() was copying 512KB unnecessarily. By using Vec::from_raw_parts to transmute the Vec<Symbol<M>> into Vec<u8> (safe because Symbol<M> is #[repr(transparent)] over [u8; M] and Copy), we avoid this copy entirely. Also separated the generic path matrix to Vec<F> to fix compilation.
asi.note: All 125 tests pass. Decode now ~183µs (2.67 GiB/s), getting closer to rlnc's ~171µs (5.7 GiB/s).

description: Remove split_at_mut in decoder Gauss-Jordan by using raw pointers

asi.hypothesis: split_at_mut in the inner loop of Gauss-Jordan was adding overhead
asi.result: No measurable change (~182.9µs vs ~182.9µs); LLVM already optimizes split_at_mut away

description: Add optimized profile with LTO/codegen-units=1 for users who want maximum performance; no code changes

asi.hypothesis: Adding an optimized profile with LTO and codegen-units=1 allows users to get better performance (decode improves ~10% to ~164µs) without affecting default release builds.
asi.note: This is a Cargo.toml-only change. Release profile numbers remain encode ~18.3µs, decode ~182.7µs, recode ~9.3µs. The optimized profile improves decode to ~164µs.

description: Final benchmark after exhaustive optimization; reached practical limit without GFNI

asi.bottleneck: Lack of GFNI for AESTowerField8b (different irreducible polynomial than standard AES). Binius has GFNI paths but requires compile-time target-feature=+gfni.
asi.optimizations_applied: Precomputed mul tables, SSSE3/AVX2/AVX-512VBMI split-table SIMD, lazy partial symbols, removed redundant init_matrix, ptr::write symbol selection, avoided 512KB copy in decode, fast-path coefficient generation with fill_bytes, separated generic matrix path, added optimized profile with LTO
asi.next_steps: Would need field isomorphism from AESTowerField8b to standard AES polynomial to use GFNI at runtime, or switch to a field representation compatible with GFNI

description: Use unchecked SIMD scale_add_assign in encoder/recode/decode_symbol hot paths; eliminate redundant scalar==0/==1 checks per coefficient

asi.hypothesis: scale_add_assign_simd checks scalar==0 and scalar==1 on every call. In the encoder/recode hot loops, the caller already knows scalar != 0 (checked in the loop). Using scale_add_assign_simd_unchecked skips these redundant checks.

description: Use unchecked SIMD in decoder Gauss-Jordan scale/scale_add_assign; cumulative ~1-2% encode, ~1.7% decode, ~8.6% recode vs baseline

asi.hypothesis: Eliminate redundant scalar==0/==1 checks in decoder Gauss-Jordan by using unchecked SIMD wrappers
asi.note: Variance is high (encode 17.7±0.3µs, decode 179.6±1µs, recode 9.5±0.4µs). Cumulative improvement from before unchecked SIMD changes: encode ~1.2%, decode ~1.9%, recode ~8.6%.
asi.next_action_hint: Explore flattening encoder data storage or inlining Symbol wrapper to match rlnc's flat Vec<u8> layout

description: Revert flat Vec<u8> encoder data experiment (worse encode); keep unchecked SIMD in hot paths

asi.hypothesis: Flat Vec<u8> with chunks_exact(M) in encoder hurt performance (~18.4µs vs ~17.2µs). The Symbol<M> wrapper is already zero-cost due to #[repr(transparent)] and Copy.
asi.flat_data_result: Worse encode performance; LLVM optimizes Symbol iteration better than chunks_exact
asi.next_action_hint: Remaining gap is small. Focus on micro-optimizations in decoder coefficient matrix ops or try parallel encode for very large symbol counts.

description: Eliminate redundant check_rank_increase in decoder add_symbol; incremental_rref_update now correctly returns rank increase bool

asi.hypothesis: Decoder add_symbol called check_rank_increase (elimination on scratch_row) before pushing, then incremental_diagonalization called add_row_unchecked which ran incremental_rref_update (elimination on actual matrix row). This doubled the coefficient matrix work. By having incremental_rref_update return bool and removing the explicit check_rank_increase from add_symbol, we eliminate the redundant work.

description: Final state after eliminating redundant check_rank_increase in decoder add_symbol

asi.hypothesis: Decoder add_symbol no longer calls check_rank_increase before pushing; instead incremental_diagonalization pops redundant rows. This eliminates double elimination of coefficient rows.

description: Cache is_aes flag in RlnDecoder to avoid repeated TypeId checks in recode/decode/decode_symbol/gaussian_elimination

asi.hypothesis: Repeated TypeId::of::<F>() checks in hot paths (recode, decode_symbol, gaussian_elimination) add small overhead. Caching a boolean flag during configure() eliminates this.
